motivation.quote: Longitudinal studies invest heavily in collecting and curating their data, yet machine learning is either left aside or applied as if every wave were an unrelated feature. We built Long-Toolkit so that experts of longitudinal studies can get their data ready, and measure fairly whether conventional or longitudinal machine learning is worth it.
motivation.attribution: Simon Provost (McGill University) & Dr Alex Kwong, LEAP lab (University of Edinburgh)

tutorial_steps.title: Step 1: Stage A (Data Preparation)
tutorial_steps.goal: Use the data preparation tools to generate synthetic longitudinal data with controlled temporal patterns, or to convert cohort files between CSV, Parquet and Stata formats.
tutorial_steps.outcome: Output: prepared longitudinal dataset(s) ready for preprocessing.
tutorial_steps.recommendation: When no built-in tool fits a dataset, write a custom script and consider opening a pull request.

tutorial_steps.title: Step 2: Stage B (Data Preprocessing)
tutorial_steps.goal: Use the data preprocessing tools to clean, impute, harmonise and reshape longitudinal datasets so they are ready for modelling.
tutorial_steps.outcome: Output: quality-checked dataset(s) ready for modelling.
tutorial_steps.recommendation: When no built-in tool fits a dataset, implement a custom workflow and consider opening a pull request.

tutorial_steps.title: Step 3: Stage C (Machine Learning)
tutorial_steps.goal: Use the benchmarking tools to compare standard and longitudinal machine learning under one shared protocol, and establish whether machine learning, and/or longitudinal machine learning, is worth it on a dataset compared with a statistical baseline. Training tools sit alongside them.
tutorial_steps.outcome: Output: saved models, benchmark rankings and evaluation summaries ready to explain or share.
tutorial_steps.recommendation: When no built-in tool fits a dataset, run a custom machine learning pipeline and consider opening a pull request.

tutorial_steps.title: Step 4: Stage D (Explainability)
tutorial_steps.goal: Use the SHAP analysis tool to explain a saved model, e.g., the best estimator of a benchmark, and see which features drive its predictions.
tutorial_steps.outcome: Output: SHAP values, feature-importance figures and report artefacts ready to share.
tutorial_steps.recommendation: When no built-in tool fits a model, run a custom explainability analysis and consider opening a pull request.
